voyage.name: Bike Tours of Lima
voyage.price: Biking tours US$35–US$90, other prices vary, pay in U.S. dollars
voyage.content: A variety of 'public' and private bicycle, walking and food tours of Lima by English-speaking guides. Prior booking is required. It is the number 1 activity in Lima on Tripadvisor.

voyage.name: The Lima Gourmet Company
voyage.content: A combined city and culinary tour of Lima. Travellers will visit a local market, have a hands-on cooking class and try different Peruvian dishes while they tour the city's main districts and historical points of interest. Great if you don't have much time in Lima.

voyage.name: Exquisito Perú
voyage.price: $59 to $159 depending on the food tour
voyage.content: Explore Peruvian gastronomy through fun and interactive walking food tours in different parts of the city. Also available in Arequipa and Cusco.

voyage.name: Folkloric dance shows
voyage.hours: Almuerzo: Fri Sat 13:00–17:30; Noches de Foclore: Tue Wed 21:00–00:15; Thu 21:45–01:35; Fri Sat 22:00–14:00
voyage.content: Live shows of local dance with dinner or lunch included. Choose between Almuerzo (lunchtime) Shows, Noches de Folclore (folklore evenings) and periodic special shows.

voyage.name: Mirabus bus and road train tours
voyage.price: Most bus tours: adults S/70, children (4–10 years) S/50, under 4s free. City centre road train: adults S/5, children (4–10 years) S/3, under 4s free. Other prices S/10–220 per person.
voyage.address: Tourist information booth in Parque Kenedy, Miraflores
voyage.content: Various themed day and night bus tours of Lima and the surrounding region, including excursions to Caral and Pachacamac. They also operate a road train around the main sights of Centro.

voyage.name: Biblioteca del Parque Municipal
voyage.content: A good first stop as the Oficina de Turismo is located here.

voyage.name: El Funicular
voyage.content: Exhibitions of art and photography.

voyage.name: Feria Gastronomica
voyage.address: Corner of Av. El Sol Oeste and Av. General Jose de San Martin
voyage.content: Sale of various traditional dishes.

voyage.name: Parque Municipal
voyage.address: Corner of Av. Pedro de Osma and Av. Almirante Miguel Grau
voyage.content: Park and main square of Barranco.

voyage.name: Paseo Saenz Pena
voyage.content: Historical buildings, gardens and several art galleries can be found here.

voyage.name: Plazuela Chabuca Grande
voyage.content: It is a place dedicated to the memory of the singer Chabuca Granda.

voyage.name: Sala de Exposicion del Patrimonio Industrial
Museo Galería Arte Popular de Ayacucho
Museo de la Electricidad
voyage.content: In addition to exhibits featuring the use of electricity, the museum also covers the history of Lima's trams and runs a restored tram Tu-Su 10:00-17:00. Adults S/2, children S/1. The tram runs between the Museo de la Electricidad and the Museo de Osma, traveling along Av. Pedro de Osma between Calle Castilla and Calle Montero Rosas.

voyage.name: Museo Pedro de Osma
voyage.content: Arte Colonial.

voyage.name: MATE Asociación Mario Testino
voyage.content: A non-profit cultural organization focused on the work of the photographer Mario Testino. After 35 years living abroad, it was the personal desire of the artist to bring the largest collection of his work to Lima, his hometown, in contribution to the cultural heritage of Peru.

voyage.name: A Todo Tren
voyage.content: A 30-minute tour departing from Parque Municipal.

voyage.name: Sentidos Thai
voyage.price: Traditional Thai massage: 1 hour S/75, 1½ hr S/105, 2 hr S/130. Therapeutic Thai massage: 1½ hr S/115
voyage.content: Sentidos Thai is the only Thai massage salon in Lima. Both traditional and therapeutic Thai (Yoga) Massage are offered. All masseurs have been certified in Thailand. Reservation via email or phone is required.

voyage.name: Central Restaurante
voyage.content: Central offers an eye-catching menu with inspiration from all parts of Peru.

voyage.name: Cala
voyage.content: Seafood, grill, wine.

voyage.name: El Hawaiano
voyage.content: Buffets, Italian, Japanese, plenty of seafood, sculptures made from fruit.

voyage.name: Puro Perú
voyage.content: Peruvian food including sushi, ceviche, criollos and grill.

voyage.name: Viejo Fundo
voyage.content: Grilled meat, seafood and pasta.

voyage.name: Isolina
voyage.content: Great Peruvian restaurant with impressive service.

voyage.name: Canta Rana
voyage.content: Fresh scallops with the Peruvian version of Parmesan, and your choice of drink to go with it.

voyage.name: Damajuana
voyage.content: It's like a dinner buffet show with some interesting performances.

voyage.name: El Tizon'
voyage.content: Here you can do some shots of this or that and also order some food if you get a case of the munchies.

voyage.name: El Dragón
voyage.content: High adrenaline disco dance and nightclub.

voyage.name: La Noche de Barranco
voyage.content: Mondays jazz, most other nights rock.

voyage.name: 3B, Barranco`s Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: TV, Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: B Arts Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: B Arts Boutique Hotel, arts-boutique hotel opened in 2013, features 17 suites and a signature restaurant by Oscar Velarde.

voyage.name: Barranco Backpackers Inn
voyage.content: Breakfast, Internet, book exchange.

voyage.name: The Point - Lima Hostel
voyage.content: Breakfast, pool table, table tennis, Wi-Fi, hot water.

voyage.name: Second Home Peru
voyage.content: Pool, hammocks, garden, Wi-Fi, mini-bar.

voyage.name: Fortaleza del Real Felipe
voyage.content: Constructed in 1747. This fort was built to protect Lima from pirates during the viceroyalty period, and then featured prominently in the defense of the emerging new nation against Spain in 1866.

voyage.name: Museo de la Fuerza de Aviación Naval
Museo Naval
voyage.price: Adults S/3; students and children S/2
voyage.content: Covers the history of the Peruvian navy. And you can walk along the promenade in front and even take a short cruise in the harbor (extra fee).

voyage.name: Museo de Sitio Naval Submarino Abtao
voyage.content: An old submarine that you can go inside, built in 1952 by American Electric Boat company, purchased by Peru in 1954.

voyage.name: Callao Brewing Co
voyage.content: Their Pilsen beer is sold in bottles and cans throughout Lima.

voyage.name: Villa La Punta
voyage.content: A bed & breakfast out on La Punta (the peninsula that projects out into the Pacific from the rest of Callao).

voyage.name: Seamen's Club Perú
voyage.content: A colonial house fashioned into a guest house by the sea.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Lima Airport
voyage.address: Ave. Tomas Valle S/N Esq Ave
voyage.content: A handy place to stay if you want to be by the airport, at a price, naturally. Includes indoor pool, airport shuttle, restaurant/bar, and breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: Pay Purix
voyage.address: Av. Bertello Bolatti (Intersections Avenues Japón and Bocanegra), Av. Japón (Ex Bertello), Mz. F, Lote 5, Urb. Los Jazmines, 1ra. Etapa
voyage.content: 8-min walk from the airport, a very cheap taxi ride, or you can use their pickup service. Private rooms available. This hostel has a cool yet clean vibe to it with a bar in the back. The owner is very helpful and make sure to ask him the easy way to get to Lima Center (you will save a lot of taxi fares).

voyage.name: Hotel Costa del Sol Lima Airport
voyage.content: Airport hotel on airport grounds. Nearest to the airport for late arrival followed by an early departure.

voyage.name: Congreso de la Republica
voyage.content: The main seat of the Congress of the Republic of Peru. Completed in 1908.

voyage.name: Correo Central
voyage.address: Pasaje Piura, next to the Palacio de Gobierno
voyage.content: Glass-covered shopping arcade. A 19th-century copy of one in Brussels.

voyage.name: Facultad de Medicina "San Fernando"
voyage.address: Av. Grau between Huanta and Cangallo
voyage.content: Part of the National University of San Marcos, the building requires ID for entry. There is a botanical garden at the rear, and some nice old buildings.

voyage.name: Hotel Bolivar
voyage.content: Visited by the likes of John Wayne and Orson Welles in times gone by.

voyage.name: Convento de San Francisco
voyage.alt: Museo del Convento de San Francisco de Asis de Lima, The Franciscan Monastery or Catacombs
voyage.content: Fans of colonial churches will be pleased with the architecture of this well-known church in downtown Lima. voyage.name: Catedral de Lima
voyage.content: Construction began in 1535 and completed in 1649. It is dedicated to St John, Apostle and Evangelist.

voyage.content: An interesting collection of popular arts, including masks and costumes from current festivities in the Andean region. The Institute is housed in a very old colonial townhouse. One of few of its kind open to the public.

voyage.name: Museo del Banco Central de Reserva
voyage.address: Jr. Ucayali 271 (corner of Jr. Lampa and Ica)
voyage.content: A representative sample of Peruvian art of all time, from millenary times to the 21st century: archeology, traditional folk art and republican painting rooms. The beautiful former central bank building was completed in 1929.

voyage.content: Features a large fountain, Japanese gardens, Teatro La Cabana. Museo Metropolitano de Lima is in the south east corner and Museo de Arte de Lima is in the north of the park.

voyage.name: Parque Juana Larco De Dammert
voyage.address: Bordered by Garcilaso de la Vega, Paseo de la República and 9 De Diciembre
voyage.content: Features a fountain and is home to the Museo Militar and the Museo de Arte Italiano.

voyage.name: Parque de la Reserva
voyage.address: Bordered by Paseo de la República, Sanchez Cerro, Arequipa and Madre de Dios with Petit Thouars running right through the middle
voyage.content: Re-opened on July 27, 2007, with 13 fountains and a Guinness World Record for the highest public fountain at over 80m tall. Best time to go is right at sunset and stay till dark to see all the lights in full effect in each one of the fountains. The laser show at the Fuente de la Fantasia fountain lasts about 30 minutes.

voyage.name: Parque Universitario
voyage.address: Intersection of Abancay and Nicolás de Piérola
voyage.content: Features three monuments and a clock tower. There is some street art across the street from the southeast corner of the park.

voyage.name: Plaza Mayor
voyage.content: This is the main square of downtown Lima. In the Spanish tradition, it's bordered in four sides by Government/Presidential Palace or Palacio de Gobierno, the Cathedral and Archbishop's Palace, the Municipalidad or City Hall, and assorted businesses.

voyage.name: Plaza Bolognesi
voyage.content: A large round park with a statue in the center, surrounded by curved buildings. A few blocks west of Parque de la Exposición.

voyage.name: Plaza Dos de Mayo
voyage.content: A large round park with a statue in the center, surrounded by curved buildings. Similar to Plaza Bolognesi.

voyage.address: 9th block of Jirón de la Unión
voyage.content: A beautiful plaza in the historical district of Lima. A walk along Jirón de la Unión will take you to the Plaza de Armas and past many historical buildings.

voyage.name: 1900 Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: It's the only hostel in the Historic Center and in front of the Museum of Art. It is in a fantastic colonial mansion. It blends the comfort of new amenities and services with the old charm of colonial architecture. It's clean and with English speaking and well-educated staff which is really helpful in a city where not many people speak English.

voyage.name: Gran Hotel Bolivar
voyage.address: Jr. De La Union 958, Centro Histórico
voyage.content: The cocktail Pisco Saur was invented here. Royalty stayed here, and the Rolling Stones had to leave for bad behavior.

voyage.name: Hotel Continental
voyage.price: Single about S/100, double about S/140
voyage.content: Looks nice, in central Lima.

voyage.content: Traditional hotel with wide range of accommodation options. Lots of rooms including dorms starting at 18 soles/night, although prices for all rooms have almost doubled in the past year. Internet cafe and travel help on site. Rooms a bit outdated at times but decorated with paintings, a minimal amount of furniture and the occasional Greek statue. This family run hotel/hostel is full of greenery and generally has guest

voyage.content: A large, very good value hotel located in the Santa Beatriz neighborhood, near to the water fountain park. One block from Arequipa, the boulevard that runs between downtown and San Isidro/Miraflores. A large supermarket, cinemas, bars and restaurants are a few blocks away. Clean, modern rooms with cable TV, WiFi, etc available for S/40.

voyage.name: El Sol
voyage.content: Clean, modern rooms with cable TV and WiFi.

voyage.name: El Parque Zoológico de Huachipa
voyage.content: A zoo with over 200 species bordering on Río Rímac. In a rather dusty, industrial part of town but pleasantly surprising once inside. Animals are well kept. Monkey islands, big cat enclosures, a large walk through aviary, penguin pools with underwater windows and bridges above. For an extra S/3 (children S/2) walk through the time tunnel to the land of dinosaurs.

voyage.name: Puruchuco
voyage.price: Tickets grant you entry to the ruins, the museum and include a small booklet. Adults S/5, students S/2, children S/1
voyage.address: Carretera Central Km 4.5, Ate Vitarte. A short distance north of Estadio Monumental. The entrance is to the right of the park inbetween Paris and Helsinki.
voyage.content: Puruchuco (feather hat in Quechua). Museum and archeological site. The museum features ceramics, quipus, wool, cotton, needles, cloth, wooden carvings, burial sacks, head dresses.

The site is littered with garbage. There is a security guard on a motorbike onsite for your safety and the safety of the ruins. It is in a unique vice-royal mansion of the 18th century built over a 7th century pre-Columbian pyramid, and is surrounded by beautiful gardens. voyage.content: The park is home to the zoo and botanical garden of Lima, the ancient city of Maranga and the museum of Ernst W. Middendorf. There's a lot to see here, everything from hippos to mummies.

voyage.name: Cruise
voyage.content: To Islas Palomino (Palomino Islands are located at short distance from the port of Lima, Callao. These small islands are inhabited by small colonies of sea lions, Peruvian boobies and Guanay cormorants. This is a reasonable alternative excursion to the famous Ballestas Islands in Paracas if you are spending some days in Lima and can not travel south to Pisco and Paracas, and also if you want to swim with the sea lion

voyage.name: Surfing
voyage.content: The city of kings is one of the few South American capitals in front of the sea and it happens to be inbetween different sea currents. Lima is a paradise for surfers and those that love seafood. Lima´s cuisine is considered one of the best and more diverse in the world.

voyage.name: Lima Golf Club

The restaurant looks like an art gallery decorated with fine colonial sculptures, and the terrace has a beautiful view of the museum and gardens. Seafood, beef, lamb, soups, pasta, options for vegetarians and choices for children (pizza, burgers).

voyage.name: Iglesia Matriz
voyage.content: This temple is the work of the architect Ricardo Malachowski and was completed in 1930. It has a neo-colonial style façade. It is decorated with a series of stained glass windows alluding to the life of Christ.

voyage.name: La Tarumba
voyage.content: Circus group with headquarters in Miraflores but they do shows all over Lima, check their website for details.

voyage.name: Luis Miro Quesada Garland Hall
voyage.alt: Galeria de la Municipalidad de Miraflores (Miraflores Municipal Gallery)
voyage.address: Municipality building, corner of calle Virgen Milagrosa and avenida Larco, opposite Parque Central
voyage.content: One of the most popular art galleries in Lima. The exhibition rooms are spacious, and the exhibitions themselves are generally very good. Work on show is mainly by local artists, with the occasional foreign contribution. Artists who display their work here usually go on to acquire a good reputation in the national art scene. Calle Virgen Milagrosa, also known as Paseo de los Pintores, often has art on display and for

voyage.name: Parque John. F. Kennedy
voyage.content: Kennedy Park, also known as the Cat Park, is famous for the many cats that reside there. You can also get amazing Picarones in Kennedy Park and on the weekends they do Salsa lessons in the park that are mostly attended by seniors. If you walk by, chances are you'll get invited. The park is right at the center of the Miraflores nightlife, with fast food places, a cinema and many bars.

voyage.name: Pucllana
voyage.alt: Museo de Sitio Huaca Pucllana, El Parque Histórico Cultural Pucllana, Huaca Pucllana o Juliana
voyage.content: Huaca Pucllana dates back to 200-700 AD. Made from small handmade, sun-dried brick, this huge construction is 22 m high. It is divided into two areas, for ceremonial and administrative ends. Guided tours include a visit through the museum, the small park with native flora and fauna and the craftsmen's house where handicrafts are on exhibit and for sale. There is also a restaurant on the site itself which although exp

voyage.content: Showcases Peruvian textiles.

voyage.content: Tandem flights for a duration of about 10 minutes. There are also courses available and locations other than Miraflores.

voyage.name: AeroXtreme
voyage.content: Tandem flights over Miraflores, one day courses at Lurín.

voyage.name: PeryFly

voyage.content: Paragliding and hang gliding.

voyage.content: Paragliding and hang gliding.

voyage.content: One of the many surfschools on Makaha beach.

voyage.name: Skate Park
voyage.content: A few pipes, a bowl and some other stuff.

voyage.name: BMX and Mountain Bike Track
voyage.content: A dirt track with jumps.

voyage.name: Larcomar
voyage.content: It's like a mall, where you can eat, shop, go to the cinema, it even has two nice night clubs. The nightclubs are open Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays, and in summer (January and February) also Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Larcomar's principal attraction is its location. It is in Miraflores, on a high hill where you can see the beach while eating or just walking. Best to visit during the sunset. Brands include Adidas, D

voyage.name: EDO sushi bar
voyage.content: In Miraflores, San Borja and San Isidro.

voyage.name: GianFranco Caffe
voyage.content: Cafe with delicious ice-cream and excellent Italian pizza. A great meeting place for Italian citizens.

voyage.name: La Lucha Sangucheria
voyage.content: A well-established sandwich place with good juice.

voyage.name: Te Burbuja
voyage.content: A small Taiwanese joint close to Parque Kenedy, with nice fruit salads, all sorts of bubble tea, fruit juices and shakes.

voyage.name: Fuzions
voyage.content: Peruvian cuisine. This low-budget restaurant just off Larco Street is pretty basic but has tasty food and is visited mostly by locals. Ask for the menu.

voyage.name: El Estragon
voyage.content: Low-budget Peruvian cuisine. This restaurant serves basic but tasty Peruvian cuisine at a reasonable price. Ask for the menu.

voyage.name: Mama Olla Restaurant
voyage.content: Peruvian cuisine - tasty food, great pisco sours, nice service.

voyage.name: Punto Azul
voyage.content: Peruvian cuisine. Nice spot to try Peruvian food. Recommendation is "Piqueo Azul.

voyage.name: Tanta
voyage.content: Peruvian cuisine.

voyage.name: Tierra Santa
voyage.content: Kebab, hummus and other Turkish specialties. They have an area where you can smoke waterpipe.

voyage.name: Rustica
voyage.content: Pizza & parilla.

voyage.name: Bembos
voyage.content: Bembos is the Peruvian version of McDonald's. They add avocado and banana to some burgers. It's really good.

voyage.name: Alfresco
voyage.content: serving "Lima's best cerviche" for around S/30. A delightful, upmarket restaurant.

voyage.name: Costanera 700
voyage.content: Owner chef Sato. One of the best restaurants in Lima whose chef was once the personal chef to former Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori. Close to the beach and excellent, excellent food. Pass on the Pulpo a la oliva (unless you like your squid in black olive sauce). Try the famous Tiradito Costanera (raw fish slides in lemon juice) or Chita a la Pimienta (fish on pepper).

voyage.name: La Gloria
voyage.content: Mediterranean/Peruvian fine dining.

voyage.name: La Rosa Nautica
voyage.content: Built over the ocean beneath Larcomar, it may be one of the best restaurants in Lima. Although quite expensive, the ambience and cuisine are superb. The entree "La Rosa Nautica Style" comes highly recommended.

voyage.name: Las Brujas de Cachiche
voyage.content: Very good traditional Peruvian dishes.

voyage.name: La Trattoria de Mambrino
voyage.address: Av. Malecón de la Reserva 610, Int. 102
voyage.content: Italian restaurant.

voyage.name: Mangos
voyage.content: Peruvian seafood. This restaurant in shopping center Larcomar has amazing views over the Pacific Ocean and serves a good Ceviche mixto.

voyage.name: Rafael
voyage.content: Peruvian fusion/haute-cuisine. Try the Lomo Saltado.

voyage.name: Café de la Paz
voyage.content: Is another excellent choice, right in front of the Kennedy Park. Peruvian-French food, in a very trendy, bohemian atmosphere. Excellent Pisco Sour.

voyage.name: Downtown
voyage.price: S/50 to get in. Some days of the week it's free entrance
voyage.content: This gay club, nicknamed Vale Todo ("anything goes") lies in the heart of Miraflores and is usually one of the last clubs to close in Lima.

voyage.name: Coffee time Miraflores
voyage.content: Handmade Peruvian coffee.

voyage.name: La Postreria Café
voyage.content: Coffee and sandwiches

voyage.name: Arabica
voyage.content: They have excellent premium Peruvian coffee.

voyage.name: Cirque Hostel
voyage.content: Cirque is a small but cozy 6-room hostel. Free breakfast and wifi, kitchen, three common areas (TV-room, terrace, and garden), bar, airport pick-up, 24-hour hot showers and reception, as well as safety lockers and bikes for rent. The hostel is a few blocks away from the beach, local food markets and Huaca Pucllana ruins. It is also the only hostel in Lima officially providing a camping site. You can pitch your tent i

voyage.name: Pariwana Backpacker Hostel
voyage.content: Hostel in front of the main Miraflores park, with a great view. 24 hours reception, bilingual staff, full guest kitchen, comfortable common areas, free breakfast, TV room, free internet and WiFi, security lockers with built-in electronic outlets, surfboard and bike rentals.

voyage.name: Pirwa Hostel
voyage.content: Good location in Miraflores. Comfortable beds, free breakfast, and a nice relaxing garden.

voyage.name: 151 Backpackers Hostel B&B
voyage.content: Fully renovated 1920s house. Private rooms, mixed dorms, outdoor patio with grill, full kitchen for your use, internet, TV and comfortable couches and living room area.

voyage.name: Red Llama Eco Hostel
voyage.content: At Red Psycho Llama they follow sustainable practices throughout the hotel, and guests can hang out on the rooftop patio.

voyage.name: Casa del Mochilero
voyage.content: This place is more like a flat than a hostel, so it has a much more at-home and chilled atmosphere, with less than 20 beds. Was the original copied by "Mochilero Inn" next door, even down to the flags outside. Dorms from S/15, one private room with two beds. Kitchen, cable TV, internet S/2 per hour.

voyage.name: Flying Dog Hostel
voyage.content: Spacious rooms, TV lounge with DVD selection, internet, kitchen to use, friendly English-speaking Peruvian employees. Excellent doubles with private bathroom.

voyage.name: Loki Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: Loki Lima is it in the heart of Miraflores, between the buzz of Parque Kennedy and the beautiful cliff top parks of the coast. This residence is decorated with a modern Loki twist around a laid back, fun atmosphere.

voyage.name: Kokopelli Backpackers Hostel
voyage.price: From S/41 per person in 8-bed dorm to S/65 per person in double room.
voyage.content: Kokopelli was founded and run by 4 guys from Holland and Peru. Great bar on the roof, and a nice hangout area downstairs. Close to most things in Miraflores, and not a far walk to the sea. Multilingual, friendly staff. Big storage lockers, and clean rooms. Great breakfast provided at a cafe around the corner. Hot showers.

voyage.name: Thunderbird Hotel Suites & Casino
voyage.content: Adjacent you will find Fiesta Casino Benavides, a quality establishment with 3 floors of gaming space and nightly live entertainment.

voyage.name: Museo Aeronáutico
voyage.address: Base Aérea Las Palmas, Santiago de Surco

voyage.name: Museo de Historia Natural de la PUCP
voyage.alt: Universidad Particular Ricardo Palma (Facultad de Biología)

voyage.name: Museo de Oro del Perú y Armas del Mundo
voyage.address: Alonso de Molina 1100, Monterrico, Santiago de Surco (enter cdra 18 y 19 Av. Primavera)
voyage.content: Peru's gold museum contains a huge collection of gaudy, gold works. Not the best place to learn about Peruvian precolumbian cultures. A large part of a Peruvian 20,000-piece collection of gold is fake, according to the Peru's consumer protection agency. A new "branch office" has opened in LarcoMar in Miraflores that is much more focused and beautifully presented; best of all, of course, is that it is located in the m

voyage.name: Los Pantanos de Villa
voyage.address: Av. Hernando de Lavalle km 20, Chorrillos
voyage.content: 263 hectares of wetlands. 210 species of birds, 10 species of fish and some reptiles and rodents.

voyage.name: La Granja Villa Sur
voyage.address: Av. Alameda del Premio Real 397, Los Huertos de Villa - Chorrillos
voyage.content: A variety of animals and amusement rides. Parrots, snakes, fish, monkeys, goats, llamas, sheep, cows, pigs and more. Viking ship, bumper cars, water slide, etc. There are amusements for very small children and some even adults will find fun. Entry price includes all amusement rides. Feed for animals can be purchased for a small fee.

voyage.name: Biblioteca Nacional del Perú
voyage.address: Av. De la Poesía 160, San Borja

voyage.name: Museo de la Nacion
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 0900-17:00; closed Mondays, 1 Jan, 1 May and 25 Dec
voyage.address: Av. Javier Prado Este 2465, San Borja.
voyage.content: The fifth floor contains an interesting photographic display detailing Peru's struggle during the years of the Shining Path.

voyage.name: Pachacámac
voyage.content: Pachacámac is about 25 km south of Lima. It is a huge archaeological site containing pre-Inca and Inca temples (entrance fee 6 Soles). This was one of the major pilgrimage sites in South America, in the years 500-1,500. The temples are constructed from adobe and are not very well preserved. There are three ramp pyramids and a temple of the sun (the only temple which may be accessed). Due to the fragile nature of the

voyage.name: Museo de Criminalística de la Policía Nacional del Perú
Hacienda Mamacona
voyage.content: Hacienda Mamacona is located next to the ruins of Pachacámac and can be seen from the Temple of the Sun. Hacienda Mamacona is open to the public and is home to some of Peru's finest Paso Horses and hosts numerous events including the Festival del Caballo de Paso Peruano and Concurso Nacional del Caballo de Paso.

voyage.name: Hipodromo de Monterrico
voyage.address: Av. El Derby s/n, puerta 3, Santiago de Surco
voyage.content: Horse racing. Two main racetracks, one dirt and one turf. Live racing each Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday (208 race days per year, 10 races per day).

voyage.name: Los Inkas Golf Club
voyage.address: Av. Circunvalación del Club Golf los Incas 950 Monterrico
voyage.content: 18-hole golf course, tennis, gymnasium, swimming pool, restaurant, cocktail lounge.

voyage.name: Country Club de Villa
voyage.content: 18-hole golf course, tennis, squash, gymnasium, minigolf, soccer and fulbito (miniature soccer), Olympic swimming pool and two smaller pools, basketball, skate ramps, restaurant, bar, kids play area.

voyage.content: Modern shopping mall.

voyage.content: Modern shopping mall. Restaurants, bars, disco, coffee shops, rather exclusive.

voyage.name: Jockey Plaza
voyage.address: Javier Prado Este 4200 Santiago de Surco
voyage.content: A large modern shopping mall with restaurants, cinemas, lots of shops, even a cigar bar. The cinemas here generally show English films in English with Spanish subtitles.

voyage.content: Italiana
